status_or_model: ESTABLISHED as the appropriate-technology / directed-technology family. CONTESTED: the authors themselves list capital-skill complementarity and schooling-quality differences as alternatives they cannot reject.

Any projection 'built on Barro-Lee' must be sought elsewhere (the WIC series, C01-C04, is the comparable lineage).

claim: The Barro-Lee data are publicly downloadable and can be used to cross-check base-year attainment in a synthetic workbench.
status_or_model: Barro-Lee dataset downloads
direction_or_magnitude: Reconstruction/extrapolation (see C08); 5-year age groups; 15+ and 25+ series; 2021 update extends coverage to 1950-2015 for ages 15-64.

source_title: Barro-Lee Educational Attainment Dataset (website)
notes: Site read. The site asks to be cited as Barro & Lee 2013 JDE 104:184-198. No explicit licence statement was seen on the pages read - verify terms before redistributing. Useful mainly as an independent check on base-year attainment shares, not as a projection engine.

claim: A ministry can simulate cohort flows and the cost of hitting enrolment targets in a generic model, with the financing gap as the output.
status_or_model: EPSSim 2.1 (Education Policy and Strategy Simulation Model)
direction_or_magnitude: 'Demographic' simulation: school-age population -> first-grade intake -> intake rate, enrolment ratios and flow rates -> enrolments by level -> teachers, classrooms, materials -> recurrent and investment expenditure against macro/budget indicators. Enrolment targets are the independent variables; expenditure is the consequence.
magnitude_verbatim: Projected intake, enrolment and flow rates; graduates; teacher and personnel needs; classrooms and materials; recurrent and investment expenditure; budget gap; by year and scenario.
source_title: Education Policy & Strategy Simulation Model (EPSSim) Version 2.1 User's Guide
venue: UNESCO, Education Policies and Strategies series
notes: Full text read (52 pp). States that the model is generic and needs country adaptation, and warns it is not sufficient for a detailed action plan. This is the closest existing 'national education sector simulation model' and the best structural precedent for a cost-and-flow workbench.

claim: UNESCO set out a generic computer-simulation model for education planning that countries could adapt themselves.
status_or_model: UNESCO generic education planning simulation model
direction_or_magnitude: Cohort/flow simulation plus cost and finance model; three scenario modes (extrapolation, exploration, forecasting).
magnitude_verbatim: Projections of enrolment flows, teacher requirements, physical inputs and costs; worked sample projections in the annexes.
source_title: Educational planning through computer simulation
notes: Full text read (85 pp). Copyright page: 'Any part of this paper may be freely reproduced with the appropriate acknowledgement.' This is the conceptual parent of EPSSim and the best single citation for 'cohort-flow + cost simulation' as a planning method.

claim: A dynamic microsimulation can carry each individual through schooling choices and generate attainment and labour-supply projections.
status_or_model: MOSART (Statistics Norway microsimulation)
direction_or_magnitude: Dynamic microsimulation: individual life courses through start / level-and-field choice / completion / continuation, plus a module that updates attainment without enrolment; transition probabilities estimated on Norwegian register data 1999-2009; embedded in a demographic projection engine.
magnitude_verbatim: Population by educational background; labour supply by education; long-run public expenditure.
source_title: Educational behavior in the dynamic micro-simulation model MOSART
notes: Full text read (58 pp; ISBN 978-82-537-8628-5). The closest microsimulation precedent for individual-level schooling transitions, and a useful contrast: it needs linked registers, which is exactly the data a synthetic workbench would have to invent.

claim: Agent-based models have been used to model schooling transitions and district-level outcomes emerging from household decisions.
status_or_model: Agent-based model of the transition to public school choice (Chicago)
direction_or_magnitude: Agent-based: household school choice with achievement/Proximity preferences, school admission and capacity dynamics; initialised on Chicago Public Schools data.

venue: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation 17(2):3
notes: Full text read (14 pp). Models choice and sorting, not cohort attainment, so it is a docking/validation precedent rather than a projection model. Useful as evidence that education ABMs are publishable in a methods journal.
